ledger.x: c. 1000 BC: the Sabines settled the central Apennines 'around the tenth century BC', founding Reate, Trebula Mutuesca and Cures Sabini; they 'also inhabited Latium north of the Anio before the founding of Rome'. The strip of Latium north of the Anio is Sabine until Tarquinius Priscus' war (585).

585 BC: Tarquinius Priscus defeats the Sabines: 'Tarquinius returned to Rome and celebrated a triumph on 13 September 585 BC'; 'In the ensuing peace negotiations, the town of Collatia was ceded to Rome'; Corniculum, Ficulea, Cameria, Crustumerium, Ameriola, Medullia and Nomentum 'submitted to Roman administration'…
505-504 BC: 'there was war between republican Rome and the Sabines'; Publius Valerius Poplicola 'celebrated a triumph over both the Sabines and the Veientes in May 504 BC'.
May 504 BC: the triumph ends the war.
475 BC: 'the Veientes and Sabines commenced hostilities against Rome'; the Sabine army 'was camped outside the walls of Veii'.
475 BC: Roman victory, 'giving Rome the overall victory'; Valerius' triumph on 1 May.
449 BC: Rome defeated 'the Sabines in an unknown battle in 449 BC'.
449 BC: the battle is the last dated Sabine war; the Sabines page has no later wars until 290.
290 BC: 'Manius Curius Dentatus conquered the Sabines.
